review.summary: Phase 8 (Qualification and delivery) is substantively met for reviewed source 68cd8aa9, which is a narrow, well-evidenced correction of CI's locked dependency-input preparation after remote run 11 failed its 60th gate command. I verified the gate rather than the prose: docs/checks/phase-08.json binds source_sha256 68cd8aa9…, source_unchanged true, passed true, checked_at 2026-10-17T14:05:35Z, and I recounted 77 recorded checks with exit_code 0 and no timeout, matching the families tools/check_phase.py commands_for(8) composes (phases 1/3/4/5/6/7 plus 29 phase-8 commands). The SDK runtime is genuinely untouched, not merely asserted: scripts/check-rust.py's rustInputsSha256 is byte-identical (b15bb1a4…) in docs/checks/phase-08-rust-1.99.0-all.json:5 and in the preserved attempt-07 report docs/checks/phase-08-accepted-attempt-07/phase-08-rust-1.99.0-all.json:5, so the delta is ci.yml, CI.md, PLATFORMS.md and one test_ci.py guard. The fix is causally proven, not assumed: docs/checks/phase-08-cold-cargo-inputs.json:1294-1389 is an actual empty-CARGO_HOME reproduction where four target-filtered fetches succeed, offline all-feature metadata then fails on uncached bumpalo 3.20.3, an unfiltered `cargo fetch --locked` repairs the same cache and metadata resolves 206 packages; docs/checks/phase-08-exact-ci-preparation.json:8-10 executes the exact extracted workflow block from a second empty cache, and docs/checks/phase-08-cold-prepared-audit.json:4-52 then passes the real dependency checker against that cold cache (fresh RustSec head 64f92cdc, 0 vulnerabilities, 0 warnings, 206 packages, no policy exceptions). Contract completeness is real and fail-closed: 448/448 implemented, contract-verified and complete-option-parity with unexplainedGaps 0 (contracts/qualification.json:53-67), namespaces uniformly crate-rooted and bound to their source module by tools/test_native_operations.py:12-28, and spot-checked contractTests resolve to actual `fn` items. Package qualification is actual: the extracted archive runs 145 minimal and 201 all-feature unit tests plus examples, 11 doctests and the external 3,820-probe consumer (docs/checks/phase-08-package-1.99.0.json:679-717), with --require-clean enforcing a fully clean tree (scripts/check-package.py:109-110). Platform labels are honest and now newly supported by a directly captured remote GNU all-feature 1.89.0 job (docs/checks/phase-08-ci-run-11/matrix-capture-receipt.json:19-28). The private selected-value scan was re-run against this exact source with zero matches (docs/checks/phase-08-private-material.json:3-12), and the attempt-07 default-build-directory low is genuinely closed by actual execution (docs/checks/phase-08-default-cargo-proof.json:8-17). The real shortfalls are the ones the project already labels: live mutation and cleanup chains have never succeeded (17/448 live-verified, two 400s with unestablished cause), no remote run has ever completed (runs 9, 10, 11 all failed contracts-and-package), and this source still needs its push, two clean-archive proofs, a new remote run and the tag — all of which by construction follow this review. I found one new substantive issue: the dependency checker still discards the child Cargo stderr and its whole report on early failure, which is exactly why run 11's root cause remained unobserved. No blocker or high finding.

findings.description: Milestone 8's "controlled live workflows and cleanup" remains only partly satisfied. contracts/qualification.json:53-67 records 17 live-verified of 448 methods (service_contract_rejection 2, permission_prerequisite 3, unverified 426), and the receipt carries cleanupState "not_needed" (contracts/qualification.json:51) only because iam.scopes.create and gateway.workspaces.provision were rejected with 400 before any ownership existed (docs/checks/phase-08-live-attempt-06.json). The entire downstream chain — scope read/update/delete, absence verification, workspace archival and owned-binding removal — therefore has no successful service execution, and the 400 cause is unestablished with an SDK request-shape defect explicitly not excluded. The live receipt is also bound to runtimeInputsSha256 c4dad30a from 2026-10-16, valid only because the Rust inputs are unchanged. Nothing is promoted on offline parity and docs/STABILITY.md:22-25 does not advertise these as stable, so this is an honest scope limitation rather than a misstatement.
findings.required_fix: Keep both operations and every dependent mutation/cleanup path explicitly live-unqualified. Before any stable promotion, obtain private diagnostics for the two 400 responses, reconcile the traffic-derived IAM and Gateway provisioning request contracts against a vendor specification, and record a new source-bound receipt that actually exercises create/read/update/delete plus confirmed cleanup.

findings.description: The phase-2 limitation remote-ci-execution is due in phase 8 and is still open after three attempts. Run 9 at bde0f4e5 failed contracts-and-package, run 10 at 6fe1fac failed on repository_byte_limit, and run 11 at 72765d5 failed the 60th of 60 gate commands (docs/checks/phase-08-ci-run-11/qualification-capture-receipt.json:8-25). Remotely, at most 59 of 77 gate commands have ever passed, so the ten remaining Rust feature sets, both package checks, the four cross checks and tracing stress have never executed on a runner, and the three optional native-host jobs remain unexecuted. The reviewed source 68cd8aa9 is uncommitted (HEAD is 72765d5), so it has no remote execution, no --require-clean archive proofs and no pushed v0.1.0 tag; docs/phase-status.json:611-617 still records the tag as locally created with remote push pending. All of this is labeled accurately in docs/CI.md:119-134 and docs/RELEASE.md:84-88, and the push by construction follows this review.
findings.required_fix: After this review, push the reviewed commit, run scripts/check-package.py --require-clean on 1.89.0 and 1.99.0 with distinct ignored outputs, and retain a source-bound Forgejo run for 68cd8aa9 in which contracts-and-package completes. Only then close the remote-ci-execution limitation, push the v0.1.0 tag at its exact published source and verify the remote peel.

findings.description: The dependency checker still destroys the diagnostics for the failure class that just cost a full remote run. The offline metadata invocation is recorded into `checks` at line 126, but line 128 raises ValueError('Unable to resolve locked all-feature dependency metadata') without including any bounded child stderr, and because the exception propagates to the handler at lines 157-160 the report file is never written at all. Consequently run 11's job log contained only "Dependency qualification failed: Unable to resolve locked all-feature dependency metadata" (docs/checks/phase-08-ci-run-11/qualification-capture-receipt.json:24), and docs/phase-status.json:1308-1313 had to enumerate three hypotheses and build a local reproducer because "the exact missing CI package or Cargo message is not observed". The same discard pattern applies to every other early raise (lines 101, 107, 116, 119, 125). The new readiness probe in .forgejo/workflows/ci.yml:74 mitigates this one path by surfacing Cargo's own stderr in a raw run block, but it does not fix the checker, and check_phase.py's 16,384-character tails can only echo what the checker prints.
findings.required_fix: On every failure path in scripts/check-dependencies.py, append a bounded tail of the failed child's stdout/stderr to the raised message and write the partial report (with its recorded `checks`) before exiting non-zero, so a recurrence is diagnosable from the job log and the retained artifact. Add a tools/test_dependency_policy.py regression that forces a failing child and asserts the bounded child output appears in stderr and that a failing report is written.

findings.description: The published compatibility note is now inconsistent with the platform document in the same reviewed source. CHANGELOG.md:43-45 states "Linux x86_64 musl has native runtime evidence. Other declared platforms have explicit compile-only boundaries", while docs/PLATFORMS.md:10 records x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu as having native all-feature compiler/test/doctest execution on Rust 1.89.0, substantiated by docs/checks/phase-08-ci-run-11/matrix-capture-receipt.json:19-23. The CHANGELOG understates rather than overstates, so it is not a misrepresentation, but the two authoritative platform statements now disagree.
findings.required_fix: Update CHANGELOG.md:43 to state that Linux x86_64 musl and x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu have retained native execution evidence (with the GNU scope limited to the recorded toolchain/feature set) and that the remaining three declared targets are compile-only, matching docs/PLATFORMS.md.

findings.description: The word "doctest" in the evidence boundaries is more suggestive than the retained evidence. Every doctest in the reports is compile-only: docs/checks/phase-08-rust-1.99.0-all.json:84 shows all 11 as "- compile ... ok" (10 constructor examples plus the lib.rs example), so no doctest assertion is actually executed. The same wording appears in docs/RELEASE.md:55 for the archive proofs. This is a precision issue in otherwise unusually careful platform prose, which elsewhere distinguishes compiled from executed work.
findings.required_fix: State in docs/PLATFORMS.md:9-10 (and docs/RELEASE.md:55) that documentation examples are compiled as no-run doctests, so readers do not infer executed doctest assertions.

findings.description: The authoritative delivery ledger is degraded by pervasive missing spaces between words and numerals, which makes the one mutable record that governs delivery hard to read and easy to mis-transcribe. Examples: "run10 at6fe1fac reports46successful Rust jobs" (line 71), "Pass all77 unchanged-source checks and actual Claude review of at least9/10" (line 619), "actual_cold_cache_fix_and22ci_checks_passed_full77_running_review08_pending" (line 629), and long review_context blocks such as lines 1201 and 1313 ("passed19CI,21native-operation,20native-export and32auxiliary checks (92total)"). The file is excluded from source hashing so no gate is affected, but it is the declared progress source of truth under docs/PHASES.md:20 and is 1,498 lines of partly redundant nested history.
findings.required_fix: Normalize the digit/word spacing in docs/phase-status.json narrative fields and consider moving superseded post_delivery_corrections/historical_deliveries narratives into dated records under docs/checks/, leaving the active phase-8 entry short enough to read in one pass.

limitations: Read-only review with Read/Glob/Grep only: I could not run git, cargo, or the checkers, so I verified recorded evidence for internal consistency and cross-report agreement rather than re-executing any check. I confirmed the Rust-input fingerprint equality against the preserved attempt-07 report, but I could not compute the working tree's current fingerprint to prove it still equals 68cd8aa9 at review time.

I could not produce a diff of the reviewed source against HEAD 72765d5. My conclusion that the change set is limited to .forgejo/workflows/ci.yml, docs/CI.md, docs/PLATFORMS.md and the tools/test_ci.py guard rests on the unchanged rustInputsSha256, the modified-file list in the provided git status, and the recorded review_context, not on a computed diff.

runtime_source_sha256 c4dad30a… is used across phase status, contracts/qualification.json:48 and the live receipt, but I found no tool in the inspected set that defines it, so I corroborated the runtime-unchanged claim indirectly through rustInputsSha256 equality instead of recomputing that digest.

All remote Forgejo outcomes (run and per-job statuses, the 46 successful Rust jobs, the captured parent and matrix reports) are self-recorded receipts produced by owner-run read-only watchers whose source and hashes are retained. I performed no network calls and cannot independently confirm server state, job logs, crates.io publication, or the local v0.1.0 tag object.

Per instruction I did not open credential or tenant-registration files. Live acceptance is therefore judged only from the sanitized receipt docs/checks/phase-08-live-attempt-06.json and contracts/live-evidence.json; I cannot confirm tenant scope, least-privilege configuration, or the private recovery snapshots and diagnostics held outside the repository.

I verified the dependency, package, cross, tracing-stress and private-material artifacts and spot-checked several contract test names and the GNU/musl Rust reports, but I did not read all 77 recorded command outputs or all 448 qualification rows; my contract-completeness judgement relies on the fail-closed verifiers (tools/qualification.py, native_operations.py, native_exports.py) and their unit tests passing in the gate.

The hash chain detects stale or inconsistent artifacts; it does not cryptographically authenticate the processes that produced them. Repository writers and the invoked tooling remain trusted, as docs/PHASES.md:7 states.
